claim: For every integer \(n>5040\) with \(\omega(n)=7\), the gap \(\Delta_7(n)=e^\gamma\sum_{j=0}^{7}(\ln\ln\ln n)^j/j!-\sigma(n)/n\) has a unique global minimum at \(n=367567200=2^5\cdot3^3\cdot5^2\cdot7\cdot11\cdot13\cdot17\), and \(0.1690<\Delta_7(n)<0.1691\) there.
integrity: The divisor ratios are exact rationals; logarithm and exponential evaluations are enclosed by outward-rounded intervals; the finite exponent search and tail cutoff are included in verify_gap.py. Independent audit has not been performed.
scientific_limitations: The claim is restricted to integers \(n>5040\) with \(\omega(n)=7\) and the stated truncated Robin gap. It proves neither the unrestricted Robin inequality nor the Riemann hypothesis.
title: The sharp seven-prime-support margin in the finite Robin inequality
